# Sasapaṇḍitacariya (Cp 10)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Sasapaṇḍitacariya* ("The Conduct of the Wise Hare") is the tenth narrative in the *Cariyāpiṭaka* (Cp 1.10), the fifteenth book of the Khuddaka Nikāya [Bareau, Les récits canoniques; Ohnuma, Dissertation]. It stands as the tenth and concluding story in the opening chapter devoted to the Bodhisatta's perfection of giving (*dānapāramitā*) [Wood 2005; Ohnuma, Dissertation]. Like other stories in the collection, it is a short versified summary narrated in the first-person voice by the Buddha [Ohnuma 2007; Ohnuma, Dissertation].
The text recounts the Bodhisatta's birth as a wise hare who resolves to make an unprecedented sacrifice, declaring: "Today I will give a gift that has never been given before" [Ohnuma, Internal and External Opposition]. When approached by the deity Sakka (disguised as a wandering mendicant or brahmin seeking food), the hare leaps into a fire to offer his own roasted flesh as sustenance; however, because of the virtue of the act, the fire miraculously refuses to burn him [Ohnuma 2007; Ohnuma, Dissertation].
